label: l/i/g input at step 2-3 in sequences starting with j/e/1/z
explanation: Very sparse reset-gate unit, active almost entirely in the original phase at t=3 (85% of mass) or t=2 (14%). It never fires in the copy phase and almost never at the delimiter. The input token must be l, i or g (98% of mass), and the sequence usually starts with j or e (also 1 or z). Magnitude rises when the previous tokens are x/l/i/0 and the token two back is e/j/c (top examples: j j x [i], j e x [g], j j l [l]). The predicate covers about 83% of activations and 89% of mass but has low precision (~13%): many steps with l/i/g at t=2-3 and a j/e start stay below threshold. This suggests the unit sums token-specific contributions from the first, preceding and current tokens, which a simple predicate cannot capture. Narrowing to j/e starts plus specific prev tokens raises precision to ~45% but halves recall.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=e (+3.70), t=3 (+3.36), prev2_tok=e (+3.26), orig0=j (+3.12), prev2_tok=c (+2.66), phase=0 & in_tok=l (+2.62). Lower it: to_go=0 (-0.55), in_first=0 (-0.38).
